slides.texte_overlay:
How to get extremely good at
conversation in your 20s
Ask "how" and "why" instead of "what." "What do you do?" gets a job title. "How did you end up doing that?" gets a story. Stories are where every good conversation actually lives.
Share before you ask. Instead of "Do you like travelling?" try "I just got back from Porto and I'm still thinking about the food. Where's the best place you've been?" You give first, they open up.
Use their words back. If they say a trip was "chaotic," ask "Chaotic how?" It shows you caught the detail, and it pulls the best part of the story out of them without any effort.
Have a few stories ready. One funny, one embarrassing, one weird. Under a minute each. Everyone has moments where the chat dips, and a good story brings it back to life every time.
Feed your head a little every day. Five minutes of history, art or science gives you endless things to talk about. Curious people never run out of conversation.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: "So, what do you do?" and then silence. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Now I never run out of things to talk about.

slides.texte_overlay: Disagree with a smile. "No way, I think pineapple on pizza is genius." Light disagreement makes a conversation fun. Agreeing with everything makes it feel like talking to a polite wall.
Know how to end well. "I've got to run, but this was great. Let's pick it up next week." Ending on a high leaves people wanting more, and that's exactly how good conversations turn into friendships.
